title: Top 3 most underrated exercises
summary: NH names his three most underrated movements: the lying pullover, the properly performed dumbbell row, and the bench-supported 'Arnold raise' for side and rear delts. All are sustainable weekly for life with low injury risk and target the V-taper, upper back and round shoulders most people want but rarely program.
claims: The pullover changed his physique more than anything: it made him look wider, flared his lats and also helps arms and chest
The pullover is one of the best upper-body movements and the best complement to the bench press
Nearly everyone can do pullovers, with many variations: dumbbell, EZ bar, barbell, supinated, incline, cable
Do pullovers lying down rather than standing so the weight pulls on the arms, thoracic spine and upper back
He believes pullovers expand the ribcage by spreading the cartilage between the ribs, besides growing the lats
Stiff shoulders can limit pullover range; start light and build mobility
Keep the back of the shoulders supported on the bench during pullovers to avoid shoulder instability
Start pullovers with 3 sets of 6-10 once a week to build mobility, then you can be greedy; he does them every two days as nucleus overload
Dumbbell rows are underrated because people favor barbell rows, and most who do them just go down and up without using the whole upper back
Done properly, dumbbell rows hit the back without involving the lower back or posterior chain and can be done weekly without structural damage
Pullovers and dumbbell rows are versatile enough to fit anywhere in a session
Lateral and bent-over raises often overuse the traps and can hurt the shoulder as load rises
Arnold raises on a bench allow lighter weight, strict form and no cheating, and are easy to recover from; they can be done twice a week for big shoulders
Varying grip on dumbbell rows can shift emphasis to traps, lats or rhomboids
Most programs for people wanting a V-taper and round shoulders lack these movements and are only squats, deadlifts and benches
exercises: lie on bench, back of shoulders supported, arms extended behind

full upper-back engagement, not just down and up; vary grip
